components.source_check: Durrett p. 244: definition of uniform integrability (limit over M of the supremum of tail means) and the E(X; A) notation. Matched; the handbook restricts the definition to integrable variables, which does not change which families qualify (a non-integrable member has infinite tail mean at every M). Boundary: empty family convention (line 23) and the non-UI spike family worked in the annex lines 27-30.

Durrett p. 244: remark that UI gives sup E|X_i| at most M + 1; trivial example of a family dominated by one integrable variable; absolute-continuity step inside the proof of Theorem 4.6.1. All present with written proofs (annex lines 6-7, 22-25, 8-20); the handbook adds the converse, finite families and the failure of bounded first moments with a worked counterexample (annex lines 27-30).

Durrett p. 245 Theorem 4.6.2 with both examples (x^p, p > 1, and x log+ x) and its proof. Matched; the handbook states finiteness and Borel measurability of Phi, which only makes explicit what E Phi(|X_i|) presupposes, and adds the convex converse with a written construction (annex lines 48-72).

Durrett p. 244 Theorem 4.6.1 (all sigma-fields contained in F_o) and its proof (absolute continuity, Jensen, Chebyshev, defining identity on the event where E(|X| | F) exceeds M); the remark that UI families can be very large is conveyed by line 69-71 (no nesting or countability assumption). Matched.

Durrett p. 246 Lemma 4.6.5 (item 5, uniform in A) and the chapter-2 facts the source invokes in Theorems 4.6.3-4.6.4 (Lemma 2.2.2, Theorem 2.3.4, Exercises 2.3.4-2.3.5), each with written proof. Matched.

Durrett pp. 245-246 Theorem 4.6.3: hypotheses (E|X_n| finite, convergence in probability), all three implications, the clipping truncation phi_M for (i) to (ii) and the cutoff psi_M (x on [0, M-1], zero on [M, infinity), linear between) for (iii) to (i). Matched, with every step written.

Durrett p. 246 Theorem 4.6.4 (three equivalent conditions for a submartingale). Matched; the handbook adds the supermartingale form and the terminal inequality with written proof; the convergence step rests on the route's proved martingale convergence theorem.
Durrett p. 247 Theorem 4.6.7 (iv): an integrable X with X_n = E(X | F_n). Matched, including that the closing variable need not be F_infinity-measurable (line 127-128).

Durrett pp. 246-247 Lemma 4.6.6 and Theorem 4.6.7 (four equivalent conditions) with the source proof chain. Matched; the identification of the limit for a closing Z is proved by a written pi-lambda argument.
Durrett p. 247 Theorem 4.6.8 and its proof (tower property, Theorem 4.6.1, Theorem 4.6.7, Lemma 4.6.6, pi-lambda identification). Matched with every step written.

Durrett pp. 247-248 Theorem 4.6.9 and continuation (cited at line 174): theorem present (strengthened to L^1); the incredible reading (tail event independent of each F_n, so P(A) equals the indicator and Kolmogorov's zero-one law follows) present with written proof; the Chung line and its attribution, the obvious reading and the closing assessment are absent from the route.
components.gap: The route (body lines 161-176, annex lines 287-305) supplies Theorem 4.6.9 and the Kolmogorov zero-one argument but not the rest of the source continuation that line 174 cites as 'thm. 4.6.9 and continuation' (Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, version 5, pp. 247-248). Supply (a) the line Durrett borrows from Chung asking the reader to judge whether the result is obvious or incredible, with its attribution; (b) the obvious reading: since the indicator of A is F_infinity-measurable and F_n increases to F_infinity, the best guess of the indicator given F_n should approach the best guess given F_infinity, which is the indicator itself; (c) Durrett's closing assessment that the tail argument may not show the theorem to be 'too unusual or improbable to be possible', but that this and later applications show it is a very useful result.

defect_observations: Body lines 8-10 state that the chapter develops Durrett's Section 4.6 and the first three theorems of Section 4.7 (pp. 244-250); because of the C011, C015 and C016 omissions that claim currently overstates the route.

C012: Durrett titles Theorem 4.6.10 'Dominated convergence theorem for conditional expectations' (p. 248); the route does not record that name, and the annex proof (line 339) uses 'conditional dominated convergence' for the fixed-information result of handbook/parts/p15/conditional-expectation.tex lines 84-109, so a reader searching for the source's name finds a different theorem. Not counted as a coverage gap; unrouted owner text at handbook/parts/p15/limit-theorems-and-concentration-w02c-p15-014.tex lines 465-491 addresses it.

C019: the source's terminological note that some authors call backwards martingales reversed (p. 249) appears on the route only as the index subentry martingale!reverse (body line 329) and the phrase 'reverse-time indices'; it is not stated in the text.

Citation placement: end-of-entry citations directly follow handbook-added assertions at body lines 140-142 (the identification of the limit for a closing Z, which in the source corresponds to Theorem 4.6.8 rather than Lemmas 4.6.5-4.6.6 and Theorem 4.6.7) and body lines 351-354 (the finite-dimensional vector extension, which is not in Theorem 4.7.3). Read under the chapter's end-of-entry citation convention they cite the entry, not the added sentences; an editor may wish to make that explicit.
Body line 188 asserts |Y| at most Z almost surely; the annex proof does not write the one-step limit argument (it follows from |Y_n| at most Z and Y_n to Y almost surely). Trivial; not counted.
